title: [BugFix] Support PCP/DCP preempt offload with local block spans
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable preempt offload for supported MRV2 PCP/DCP configurations and correctly map tokens to DCP-sharded KV blocks. Existing code rejects both DCP>1 and PCP>1, and uses raw group block sizes for transfer ranges even when DCP increases the token span.

- Use `resolve_dcp_kv_block_size` for store/restore ranges, including partial last blocks and speculative-tail exclusion.
- Remove the PCP=1 restriction. Each worker transfers its own local cache; PCP expands the workers rather than the local cache's token span.
- Construct the CPU KV coordinator with `pcp_world_size=1`, matching Ascend's coordinator contract, while preserving the actual DCP size.
- Preserve the full per-engine worker count (`TP × PP × PCP`) for store completion. A single PCP slice must not mark a transfer complete.

No worker transport, circular-cache or physical buffer implementation is changed. The repository's existing MRV2/platform constraints still determine supported configurations. Related to #18090 and tracking #19663; this remains a focused alternative implementation and regression suite for vendor/community coordination.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Enables preempt offload for supported MRV2 PCP/DCP configurations and corrects DCP block-span mapping. No new option or performance claim.

### How was this patch tested?

Rebased onto main `99a8e0a0e` on 2026-10-29. The net diff is limited to the offload manager and its tests; redundant CI test rename commits are dropped.

```bash
TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 pytest -q tests/ut/kv_offload/test_preempt_offload_connector.py
# 80 passed
bash format.sh ci
# passed
git diff --check
# passed
```

Fresh zero-NPU CPU tests use the real scheduler, CPU coordinator and block pool with verified vLLM main `544f182d`. Twelve new cases cover PCP1/2/4, DCP1/2/16, TP and PP2 combinations, plus sharded and replicated KV groups. They verify CPU coordinator PCP=1/DCP=actual, partial-block store/restore without multiplying the span by PCP, speculative-tail exclusion, and waiting for completion from all PCP workers. Host-capacity probing and physical GPU transfers are mocked.

RED/GREEN control: the new twelve-case suite against the previous PCP-restricted manager yields ten expected PCP>1 failures and two passing PCP1 controls; the candidate passes all eighty tests. Existing DCP, sliding-window, Mamba, transfer-metadata and cleanup regressions remain covered.

No NPU/model service or physical cross-worker PCP transfer E2E was run for this change. The CPU results establish scheduler mapping and aggregation behavior; physical integration remains a device-validation boundary. Community CI must validate both supported release and main lanes for the new head.

Release-note policy: the fragment is omitted for this non-feature change, as requested by the contributor.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542
